snippet.title: Actors Painful Costumes In Spider-Man No Way Home
snippet.description:
They’re not always comfortable, but somehow the Spider-Man actors make it work. Many of the characters who returned from other Spider-Man universes got lucky enough to end up with much more comfortable costumes. Doc Ock was the real deal the first time around, so ditching the puppet arms for blue circles was a-ok in Alfred Molina’s books. Willem Dafoe got to ditch his mask making for a much easier time hearing and seeing on set. Jamie Foxx had never experienced really being Electro in the same way the others got to embody their characters, so his new suit made for a very different experience. 
The Spider-Man boys got to bond over some of the struggles they faced with their suits - including the fact that it was a total nightmare when any of them needed to pee! The suits were tight and restrictive as could be - and while certain aspects were integrated to help, they often wound up making the performer’s lives more difficult, restricting their breathing or movement.
The Iron-Spider suit included some special golden gauntlets and while we loved the way they looked, Tom Holland wasn’t so fond of them. The actor also faced disappointment when it came to using a smartphone wearing the lycra suit - let’s just say the fabric isn’t so touch screen friendly. Andrew Garfield was intimidated to jump back into the suit - so he made sure to prep himself for the costume fitting. Maguire had gone nearly twenty years without putting on his Spidey-Suit, so off the bat, he wasn’t feeling so confident in it, until he felt totally at home.
They can be painful and actors have different experiences with their costumes, but in the end, no pain no gain - and usually the look of these outfits on-screen are totally worth it!

snippet.title: The Voices Behind Disney's Turning Red
snippet.description:
Turning Red features the best voice talent around, from seasoned actors to popular singers, to performers totally new to the business! Who brought the heart and soul to these character voices? We’ve got the scoop on who the actors are and where they came from - along with some clips of them in action, doing what they do best in the booth.
Rosalie Chiang may be young - but she was even younger when she got this job and started the process. The actress is as inexperienced as they come, ‘Turning Red’ being the first feature film she’s ever performed in. Not a bad first gig! She got the delight of working with a seasoned and beloved veteran- the one and only Sandra Oh. One spunky actor made sure their presence was known - something anyone who’s watched ‘Never Have I Ever’ would be familiar with. Maitreyi Ramakrishnan brings her energy to one of Mei’s best friends. Ava Morris is a real-life teenager- no wonder she’s a pro at playing a teen on screen. Hyein Park is new to acting - this being her very first role - but the performer has had a longstanding relationship with Pixar in a completely different department! 
Anne-Marie, the UK singer-songwriter wasn’t feeling as comfortable as she usually does in the booth - but she made it through and managed to bring some solid work to the table. Ever heard of actress and comedian Sherry Cola? If not -after hearing her performance in this, you won’t forget her!
Then, of course, are the five boys behind the voices of everyone’s new favorite boy band- 4*town. We’ve got all the details you need on this talented crew.

snippet.title: Harry Potter Students Vs. Professors Bloopers
snippet.description:
We’re all for some Harry Potter bloopers - and this time it's not just the students. Even the Professors at Hogwarts goofed off a little bit - sometimes at the student’s expenses.

Daniel Radcliffe and Rupert Grint definitely earned the first prize for on set shenanigans - but following close behind were some of the unexpected professors at Hogwarts. Believe it or not - Snape himself had a keen liking to pulling pranks. And so did Headmaster Professor Dumbledore - though his pranks and hilarity were always in service to embarrassing Radcliffe. But Dan was obviously too busy getting injured and laughing in the halls of Hogwarts behind the scenes - to really mind it. The directors had a great laugh - just observing the bloopers unfold on camera. One even got his hands dirty for a brawl sequence - that he definitely regretted getting involved in. When the “coming of age” period came to the screen of the HP Fandom era - things just got more goofy for the cast and crew. Maybe just working so much really made them a little slap happy.

These moments with the faculty and students of Harry Potter are just too funny to pass up on. And we couldn’t help but dig into the franchise's funniest moments. So sit back and enjoy as we head into some hilarious Potter bloopers - Students Vs. Professors edition.

snippet.title: Turning Red Behind The Scenes Vs. The Real Scene
snippet.description:
Of all the things to put Toronto on the Disney map, it’s a movie about puberty. And ya know what? It’s a great movie at that! Writer and director, Domee Shi pulled her inspiration straight from some very nostalgic places. One of which was anime, and the other was boy bands. Curious to know which ones? Give the video to watch! The inspiration for Mei came straight from Domee herself. Not just character traits but also goofy things she remembers doing as a kid. This includes one scene she’s just a bit embarrassed by. There was some super awesome technology created to help with representation on screen, which is a step in the right direction! There was one cut pickup line that got replaced that you’ve just have to hear. We’ve got a little bit on the recording process for Rosalie Chiang and the band. And we also have the inside scoop on some of the earlier drafts of Turning Red. Would you believe us if we said there were gangsters at one point? And also, Mei’s red panda had an extra special ability but it was just too complicated for the animators to pull off. It’s a first for Pixar to have an all-female creative team, and the team is just stoked about it. And finally, this movie is embracing the chunky cute. They’re not shying away from the little things that make each person unique. Hopefully, future movies follow Turning Red’s lead and start implementing some of the beautiful technology and authenticity that this movie managed to incorporate.

snippet.title: The Adam Project Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
The Adam Project brings all the heart, action, and special effects we could want, so how did the whole world come together? The performances, special guests, and practical builds made major impacts in building what would become the backdrop for this heart-warming film.
One of the best parts of the movie is newcomer Walker Scobell who gave Ryan Reynolds a run for his money with his oh-so-natural improv skills. The young actor was even able to recite a Reynolds classic at the drop of a hat - Reynolds definitely met his match! Scobell had a lot of experiences being on set for his first film, including losing a whopping four teeth in some way or another. One tooth actually came out in the middle of a take! While Scobell often steals the scene, when this special pup was in the frame, it was hard to look away. Adam’s pup was none other than Birdie the golden retriever - which actor did this dog belong to!? 
Adam’s family home was one for the books - being built from the ground up in just two months in a soundstage - which nature feature was a whopping twenty-five feet tall? 
Zoe Saldaña was eager to jump on board and join the movie, but filming the pandemic made her weary - fortunately, the team had the best protocols in place. That also meant the actress spent over half her time on set in quarantine - filming for less than a full week's worth! 
There are deleted scenes, raw audition footage, and a scene that went wrong over and over again - all just a part of the adventure of bringing this special flick to the screen.

snippet.title: 15 Actors Who Felt Suffocated In Their Suit
snippet.description:
Feeling trapped, claustrophobic or suffocated in your suit or prosthetics is not an uncommon thing in Hollywood. Especially among the super heroes (Marvel and DC alike). Paul Dano, who’s playing The Riddler in the new Batman movie experienced a rude wakeup call when he realized his idea was a bad one. Cling film on his face. Can you fathom why that’s a bad idea? And his acting partner, Robert Pattinson was struggling to work with his cowl, but the whole suit was a pain. Tom Holland had a straw sticking out of the weirdest place because it was the only way he could get a drink in the spider-man suit. And what do Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield both have in common aside from playing spiderman? Nearly drowning in their suits. Stellan Skarsgård, the actor from Dune really struggled with a few crazy things about his costume that could have left him having a stroke if they weren’t addressed. Ralph Fiennes’ time as Voldemort almost had him quitting acting. Or at least, a certain type of acting. One of the older Batman movies contained a character named Mr. Freeze and some problematic battery acid. Going back even earlier, The Wizard of Oz straight-up had to replace one of the actors due some dangerous makeup. And the actors playing the live-action Ninja Turtles were not prepared to wear such heavy and complicated suits. Actors will always complain about their suits because nobody seems interested in fixing them. Can’t say we blame them. Check it out!

snippet.title: 10 Roles Tom Holland Auditioned For But Was Rejected
snippet.description:
Tom Holland has offers coming left, right and center - but that doesn’t mean the actor hasn’t had his fair share of auditions as well. Holland is the star of a major franchise, and we could’ve seen him in some other pretty big ones - like Star Wars. Before he had risen to fame, the actor auditioned for movies like November Criminals - a role that wound up being a particularly big blow. What it did do was provide a very special lesson that has affected the rest of Holland’s career. 
The actor went head to head with another famous actor - Timothée Chalamet - but for which role? And which actor was successful in booking it!? 
Even though he didn’t book it, Holland’s audition for The Jungle Book wasn’t a total loss. One very special person was a fan of his performance and let the whole world know that the Spider-Man actor's audition was a brilliant one. Tom at one point did kind of set himself up for failure with a role proposal that wound up getting turned down by Sony - ouch. 
Then some auditions could have led to some very cool projects - including one with Tom Hanks at the helm. Now one show Tom wants to be on doesn’t so much require a typical audition involving learning lines - because it’s a reality show - and you’ll never guess which one. 
Tom’s Spider-Man auditions were plentiful and most of them knocked it out of the park, but some other tapes didn’t really showcase his best work. 
His career has been so varied and as his career grows, Tom only gets better and better. What role will he play next?!

snippet.title: The Batman Actors Who Were Injured While Filming
snippet.description:
In Gotham, a day without an injury is rare. Batman actors have been brutalized over the years, injured by everything from costumes, to stunts gone wrong, to an actor going a bit overboard!
Robert Pattinson started his first Batman film with a rough start. Very soon into filming, a stunt gone wrong resulted in a broken wrist. The timing was lucky though since soon after, the production got shut down for a completely different reason. His cowl was also a struggle, feeling way too constricting and leaving the actor unable to hear or breathe very well. An in-ear headphone gave the actor a painful earful as well.
Paul Dano made his life a whole lot harder when he came up with the not-so-smart idea to get himself wrapped up in saran wrap. When Catwoman was fighting Batman, Zoë Kravitz brought her all and wound up using Robert Pattinson as her punching bag! The actress herself managed to get through production without too many serious injuries, but her lead-up to filming was far from comfortable.
Colin Farrell brought strong vibes as Penguin, but all his nerves were showing filming one of the more intense stunts in the movie. Michelle Pfeiffer brought the fire as Catwoman in her expert work with a whip, but it became dangerous for herself and those around her. The actress drew blood from at least two people on set! The 2022 ‘The Flash’ movie saw a brutal crash involving the Batcycle. While filming ‘The Dark Knight Rises,’ there was another brutal injury caused by a travel method - this time it was a parachute.
No matter how it happened, the injuries that the cast and crews of these films faced were brutal, but at the end of the day, it’s all a part of the gig!

snippet.title: 20 Scenes Actors Refused To Film
snippet.description:
TV and Film is a very sensitive industry. There aren’t many jobs that exist where you have to kiss or punch or do whacky stunts. So it’s a weird niche as far as the job market goes. This means it needs super strict rules around intimacy and safety that stray from your everyday job. Euphoria is a show where the actors are always speaking up when they don’t feel comfortable with a shot because it’s a show with a lot of nudity. But it’s also a show that can bring out the worst in people. There’s a feud going on between two actors who refused to work together. And also an actor/director feud going on. Henry Cavill has a very strong say over the script for The Witcher and he had the reunion between Geralt and Yennifer completely changed as he refused to film it as planned. In the Marvel Universe (MCU and beyond) Robert Downey Junior’s refusal to say a rather useless line at the end of Avengers prompted a whole scene that wasn’t shot until the premiere. Chris Hemsworth refused to play the straight man again. And Kirsten Dunst tried out a stunt for Spider-Man and wasn’t all that happy with the results. Did you know Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson only likes to do movies that have happy endings? That outlook on life got him the ending of a movie rewritten. Ryan Reynolds, Sandra Bullock and Drew Barrymore are among a long list of actors who refuse to do their stunts - and not for the reasons you may think! We cover all that and more in this video.

snippet.title: Disney's Turning Red Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
Disney Pixar brings all the magic and nostalgic vibes we could hope for with ‘Turning Red’! Over the course of just four years, the team built a brand new story to life - which while it does include some more magical elements - was actually majorly based on director Domee Shi’s life! 
Before animating even began, a small group from the creative team took a field trip to the zoo to get up close and personal with some real-life Red Pandas. The proportions of Panda Mei in the movie are quite far from the actual animals - but equally as cute! 
For Turning Red, many newer technologies were used - including one that had never actually been proven to work. One of the technologies brought more inclusivity than we’ve ever seen before in a Disney Pixar movie, really reflecting the world around us!
It would be a Disney Pixar flick without some new catchy tunes - and these come in the form of a 90’s boy band! Billie Eilish and Finneas O’Connell were the musical minds behind the tunes - with Finneas even voicing one of the band members! You’ll never believe the creative way that the producers approached the musicians about the gig. Filming during a pandemic meant a lot of creative solutions were key - but it also meant actors would work from anywhere - which helped bring one special performer into the movie for a not-to-be-missed cameo. Recording studios were filled up with tiny huts with windows built-in for the performers to sing together, but apart. 
No matter the challenges they faced, the ‘Turning Red’ team made sure they gave it their all, bringing this special movie to life

snippet.title: Batman Actors Physical Transformation For Their Role
snippet.description:
Just how tough is a superhero workout? It’s enough to leave anyone hurtin’, but the efforts from these actors didn’t go unnoticed. From the early days of Batman to the most recent iterations, one shared experience for the actors has been going through the wringer to achieve the fitness needed to play these roles. 
Robert Pattinson may have joked about not training, but that was far from the truth - a bland diet and grueling workouts made for wild physical transformations, but at a cost. The actor did get into the swing of it at one point but post-filming - well, let’s just say it would take him a few days to be able to move in the way he does in the movie! Zoë Kravitz went to work as well, even studying how domestic and wild cats moved around to figure out how she would move as Catwoman! Colin Farrell is unrecognizable in The Batman, but when he signed on, he had no idea that almost his entire face would be covered by prosthetics! 
Ben Affleck knew when he signed on to play the Dark Knight that the audiences would expect him to look the part - so he got to work - but it wasn’t so simple this time around. The actor, being a bit older, quickly realized just how much extra care he’d have to take with his body, tending to aching muscles and clicking joints! Anne Hathaway went crazy at the gym and kept a clean diet going so she could do all she needed to for the movie, with a major emphasis on making sure she fit into the suit!
No matter how they did it, every actor committed and brought their superhero game to the table!

snippet.title: All Of Us Are Dead Painful Makeup And Prosthetics
snippet.description:
When it comes to zombies, the Netflix hit All Of Us Are Dead knows how to do it right! The makeup and prosthetics bring both the zombie characters and the students trying to avoid becoming zombies to life in a shockingly realistic way. 
One of the biggest transformations actors went through was getting their ‘Zombie’ face. Hours were spent making sure they looked as gruesome as possible - and they could do this using various pieces of specially made prosthetic, hyper-realistic looking wounds and bruises, and a dash of fake blood! Some of the prosthetics they wore covered literally half of their face! 
It wasn’t just the students who turned zombies that got extensive makeup done. All those students battling for their lives acquired their fair share of blemishes and the makeup team brought it, with dark bruises and tiny but vicious cuts all over. Need an instant nosebleed? This crew knows how to do it - their secret weapon? A small syringe full of fake blood! While we did get a lot of realistic prosthetics, a pylon subbed for a leg at one point - far from comfortable but it worked in a pinch. 
When meal breaks came along during filming, the actors stayed in their character makeup, but they were eating human food instead of actual humans! Regardless, it made for a very interesting sight! When they called it quits for the day, the work didn’t end - in fact, there were collective makeup removal parties in their trailers! All Of Us Are Dead never saw a dull moment with this kind of production behind it.

snippet.title: Uncharted Scenes Without CGI
snippet.description:
Welcome to Uncharted - a movie that’s a visual feast for the eyes - and not just because of Tom Holland and Mark Wahlberg being front and center. The CGI elevates this film to the next level as the team safely created the wild environments and situations they find themselves in. 
Finding treasure has never felt so real - Tom Holland had many practical sets to work on - including a full-fledged ship - decked out with green or blue whenever it was needed. What Holland was experiencing every day was pretty close to what his character was doing - from spinning around wildly in the air and clinging to boxes for dear life! The sequence that saw Holland fly out the back of a plane, inspired by the original video game saw Holland pulling off some of the biggest and most impressive stunts he’s ever done - including ones that “totally broke” the actor! 
How often were the crew actually filming in exotic locations? There were days spent on real boats on the water, as well as in giant studios filled with blue screens galore ready to be transformed into worlds we could only dream of. As acrobatic and skilled as these performers are, the high-flying flips and stunts didn’t happen totally naturally - CG took care of hiding all the harnesses and wires that kept the performers safe while pushing themselves as far as they could! Mark Wahlberg was as close to flying high as he could get, sitting in pretty much the best substitute for an actual aircraft there could be on set. 
The performances, the locations, the overall design - they came together to make Uncharted a film not to be missed!

snippet.title: Batman Actors Painful Suits And Prosthetics
snippet.description:
They look tough, but wearing their complex costumes and prosthetics can be even tougher! Actors in the Batman films over the years have all faced serious struggles with their costumes. 
Pretty much every Batman actor has had the same problem - figuring out a way to go to the bathroom! Most of them needed multiple people to help them get in and out of their suits. Being in the extremely warm and claustrophobic costume caused one actor to see stars and yell that he needed to get out of it immediately! Robert Pattinson actually wore a couple of the previous Batsuits in his auditions and screen tests and all these years later, he could still smell the sweat from the other actors. The Penguin in the 2022 ‘The Batman’ film is portrayed by an unrecognizable Colin Farrell, thanks to multiple facial prosthetics and an intense pre-filming ritual. The Riddler actor brought some magic to the screen, but he paid for it. The actor struggled to breathe and found himself in some pretty serious danger, wrapped up in plastic wrap. One of the Batman’s didn’t actually wear a batsuit at all. The mocap suit he wore may have been more comfortable physically, but the actor was miserable because of how ridiculous he looked throughout the process. Gal Gadot’s physique wasn’t exactly what the team initially envisioned, so she got a heavily padded suit. When Heath Ledger played the Joker, one of his key character traits actually came about because of uncomfortable facial prosthetics that kept falling off! 
Just getting through filming with these restrictive, hot and sometimes dangerous costumes made all these actors real-life superheroes!

snippet.title: 15 Improvised Scenes In Euphoria Season 2
snippet.description:
Some of the most memorable scenes from Euphoria were actually a result of total improv! From the hilarious one-liners to the brutal arguments, Euphoria took advantage of just how skilled their actors were.
Rue’s fights with her family are next level. Both her aggressive and violent argument with her mom in the first season and with her mom and Gia in the second came from the actors themselves. These performers are close and trust each other enough to be able to let themselves go to those dark and angry places, knowing they are just acting and will take care of each other when the cameras stop rolling.
Maude Apatow is pretty perfectly cast as Lexi - especially when we see her in action backstage bringing her play to life. Many of her one-liners and even her confessional style writing were loosely based on the way the actress behaved when she was in high school and running a show! Though the stakes definitely weren’t as high then - and we doubt their budget was as big as this one! 
One actress was pushed so far by their co-star, that they wound up yelling out curse words during a take, revved up by the sass they were being served. A newbie to the scene happens to be one of the best improv talents around, many of their best parts coming directly from the actor. Euphoria is next-level intense, so when certain actors get a script that they feel is missing a bit of heat, they’ll speak up. When this does happen - you can bet that new dialogue gets improvised by both the actors and the creator of the show!
Keeping the set open to the flow has made the show that much better, letting us appreciate just how great these actors are!

snippet.title: 15 Euphoria Scenes That Were Originally Much Darker
snippet.description:
Is there ever an episode that doesn’t have us in tears or terrified for a character at some point? What’s really wild is the fact that some of what we do see on screen in Euphoria is actually the toned-down version! With the cast and crew being so flexible and changing directions whenever it feels right, a lot of scenes or even plotlines were changed to be a bit less dark - but that doesn’t mean the show lost any intensity whatsoever - that’s for sure. 
Rue goes downhill fast in the second season and it’s a tough watch - but fortunately, all hope isn’t lost. While the plan was to watch Rue continue to spiral, Sam Levinson and Zendaya made it otherwise. One actor read the original script and found themselves in tears, really upset by the content and feeling nervous about filming the sequence. They didn’t complain about it with Levinson but they did discuss it - how did he deal with the situation?
Sydney Sweeney, Minka Kelly, and Chloe Cherry have all been initially asked to show some more skin, but for one reason or another, the filming happened with clothing on - not all the time of course though. 
Some characters weren’t even supposed to have much of a journey, with a terrible fate awaiting them far too early in their stories - we’re talking about some major players in the show. How did they wind up staying alive on the show?? 
Oh and remember that locker scene with a whole lot of explicit visuals? There were way more than we can even imagine in the first place - but HBO spoke up and cut the footage - a couple of times in fact. The show is intense as is, but knowing what we see is actually a bit toned down makes us see it in a different light!

The Euphoria filming days are often long and this was no exception. We’re talking three days of intense dancing every single take. If you’ve seen the number, you’ll know what he means - there were all sorts of symbols and raucous actions that made us love the dance even more. 
It wasn’t all fun and games though. Some of the extras on the set had a brutal time, spending 16 long hours on set - resulting in a lot of people walking off- including one key cast member! snippet.title: Spider Man No Way Home Without CGI

They did such a good job, that you may not have even realized some of the elements that were actually CGI when watching the film. What part of the bridge fight between Spider-Man and Doc Ock was real, and what was digital? Marvel held nothing back when creating this film, and the product they put on screen is proof of their hard work and dedication to create a movie for the ages.

Tom Holland had a great time working with Willem Dafoe and Alfred Molina, and discussed how they reacted to how the film industry has evolved since they first appeared as Spider-Man villains. Alfred Molina was a huge fan of the way the effects were done in this movie, and both actors were extremely impressed with the highly detailed and realistic CGI.

snippet.title: Harry Potter And The Deathly Hallows CGI Breakdown
snippet.description:
The world of Harry Potter is a combination of excellent writing, spot-on directing, performances we fall in love with over and over again, and of course - CGI that brings creatures and images we never could have imagined to life! 
Some scenes required very technical and detailed CGI - when the Seven Potters were in town, you can bet special effects we brought in and were responsible for the faces we see. Sometimes dark filming conditions came in handy since the CG team was able to remove certain parts of images without even needing to cover up very much. 
When Rowena Ravenclaw floated into the scene, she was filming everything solo - acting opposite a large red “x” instead of Daniel Radcliffe. Nagini is terrifying on screen, but she wound up being pretty creepy on set as well - in the form of two human arms! 
Dementors might actually be beautiful if they weren’t so terrifying - their CG design is intricate and is built from the skeleton up. Voldemort brings lots of Dementor-like vibes himself, only with his face being captured separately. Speaking of that face - remember when it dissolves away? Ralph Fiennes made a pretty great face for the cameras, but CG animation was key to making it look so haunting. 
The attack on Hogwarts is full of CG - from making the giants look large in comparison to everything else, to fully animating the statue soldiers protecting their school. Then, of course, the famous duel - The team was on a practical set, but CG was still used for the background and all the wand light magic!
The CG is beyond impressive and helps to build the world so convincingly, making us even more obsessed with the saga!

snippet.title: Tom Holland Voicing Animated Characters
snippet.description:
Tom Holland has only voiced a handful of animated projects, mostly movies, but he does have one cute-as-can-be piggie commercial he voiced once upon a time. He’s done voice acting in both his own British accent and American, depending on the project. Despite the importance of authentic accents in Spies in Disguise, it was important for his character to have an American accent. He also used his American accent in ONWARD. Which is fair, he was acting across from Chris Pratt who is American and it would be odd to have to brothers with different accents who grew up together. You could maybe excuse it if Tom’s character grew up watching Peppa Pig. For Tom’s role of Ian Lightfoot, he took inspiration from someone close to him. Which, that isn’t the only time he’s taken inspiration. He also finds his dog, Tessa, is a good muse for a character. In Dolittle, Tom plays a dog named Pip. This is one of those times he got to use his own British accent and it coming out of the mouth of a dog is just so cute! Tom is quite the physical voice actor. He talks a lot with his hands. Tom Holland and Tom Hardy have appeared in several movies together but their characters have never physically met. Strange, right? And on the topic of not being in the same space, Tom never even met one of his costars until after the movie had premiered, where the two of them engaged in an escape room. That’s a high-pressure way to say hello! Check it out!

snippet.title: Andrew Garfield On The Set Of Spider-Man No Way Home
snippet.description:
Fans were left with the mystery of Andrew Garfield’s involvement in Spider-Man No Way Home - and now we all found our dreams to have come true. The Amazing Spider-Man himself dodged and fibbed during interviews to protect the surprise that was going to unfold. But now we found some amazing No Way Home behind the scenes moments of Andrew’s time on set - and they are all wonderful in their own way.
Jumping back into an old character as big as Spider-Man’s is definitely nerve wracking - but Garfield was all in when he knew the story and who was going to be involved. With Tom Holland and Tobey Maguire - they created a brotherhood on and off the screen that we’ve never been able to see from different versions of the same character. These enjoyable moments Andrew experienced with them are what strengthened the film’s emotional journey and even helped reignite his love for the role. With its success and fan reaction - we think his desire to keep going with the role will start some momentum to bring him back a few more times. Fingers crossed!
Will he ever come back? That’s something we will just have to hope for - but either way we were left with a great return of his character and can appreciate the time we had. But enough of the sad stuff - let’s swing into some behind the scenes!

snippet.description:
Celebs really try their best when it comes to kissing scenes but oftentimes they just miss their mark. Quite literally as was the case of one actor in All of Us Are Dead. In Tall Girls 2, it was about doing good but just not doing good enough. Cobra Kai’s Mary Mouser was giving the sass to Xolo Maridueña over how awkward his kissing skills are, but he dished it right back. The cast of Stranger Things all had their moments to freak out as other than one Kindergarten kiss, none of them had kissed anybody before so their first times were filmed and super awkward. Emma Watson’s kiss with Daniel Radcliffe was like kissing a sibling. Max Greenfield kept trying to make Schmidt randomly kiss Nick a thing. He improved it at every opportunity and Jake Johnson’s response was pretty intense. Euphoria was a lot for Jacob Elordi. Jennifer Lawrence struggled with her kiss with Chris Pratt for such a funny, yet understandable reason in Passenger. Tobey Maguire’s kiss with Kirsten Dunst in Spider-Man was super dangerous due to the rain. Outside in the rain is a terrible place to kiss, by the way. It was so bad Nina Dobrev threatened to quit Vampire Diaries if they scripted another rain kiss. How I Met Your Mother Actor, Alyson Hannigan didn’t like kissing Jason Segel, the reason may surprise you. Kit Harrington found his situation with Emilia Clarke just too weird, and not because of the incestuous plotline. And Jennifer Lawrence is in here again for a completely other reason. snippet.title: Scarlet Witch Scenes Without CGI
snippet.description:
Chaos magic, witch battles, and a whole lot of wires are all contributors to bringing Wanda Maximiff, AKA the Scarlet Witch’s powers to life! Elizabeth Olsen gives it her all in every performance. Regardless of what setting she’s actually performing in, the acting we get is top-notch. 
When 
WandaVision came along and we got to see Maximoff really embrace her Scarlet Witch powers, well you can bet the CGI did a lot of favors. From her using them to bring Vision to life to constructing her fantasy world in Westview - all those layers of CG lighting and powers were key to show just how epic this power really was. 
When Wanda made her first full movie appearance, she made sure to leave her mark, showing off her elegant and intricate hand movements as Wanda’s power choreo, with the dash of red glow included hinting at all the magic we’d see soon enough. Her power seems to know no bounds! Civil War was the perfect opportunity to show off a bit of what was to come - and her arm choreo looks VERY different without all the CG added - yet somehow, Olsen pulls it off! 
Avengers: Endgame saw one of the coolest images in the Marvel world - all the strong, powerful women side by side - and you know the Scarlet Witch was included among them, radiating power through the screen.
Seeing her performances and development throughout the MCU, especially in WandaVision has proven just how powerful both Wanda Maximoff and Elizabeth Olsen are. The Scarlet Witch vibes are strong and no doubt will bring more action and excitement to the MCU in the future.

snippet.title: 20 Encanto Behind The Scenes Secrets
snippet.description:
Encanto is the kind of movie that was made by an ensemble of people. It required a lot of minds every step of the journey. From the ever-changing plot to character designs to the improvisations to last-minute cut scenes. This movie went through a lot leading up to its premiere. First off, they made the smart decision not to do away with Julieta by Mirabel’s hand. Stephanie Beatriz (Mirabel) and John Leguizamo (Bruno) improvised a heck of a lot. We bet you can’t guess what super goofy moment came from Leguizamo’s quick thinking. There was a scene that was cut from the movie at the very last second that would have changed the ending. Coming up with Bruno’s name was a challenge for everybody. So was coming up with a plot for Isabela. The song all of you was originally twice as long and the lyrics are so heartfelt it’s just too bad they were cut. And speaking of cut, there were so, so, so many character concepts that didn’t go anywhere! One character had a secret room inside of their magical room in one design. Beatriz’s pregnancy proved to be a challenge but she powered through in the best way she knew how. Her audition song was also fire by the way. Isabela and Mirabel’s rivalry was way tenser in earlier drafts. There was a belly button budget set aside for the movie. Weird, right? The fish woman had an odd name in the script. One actor did her voice in three different languages. Like we said - it took an ensemble. Now watch the video if you aren’t already!
